data.name: Ras Al Khaimah
data.summary: No emirate income or inheritance tax. Mountains and coast; growing resort development. DIFC Courts Wills guardianship clauses cover minors resident in Dubai or Ras Al Khaimah. Cost of living lower than Dubai (not sourced).

regimes.name: UAE tax residence (no personal income tax)
regimes.description: Federal level: no personal income, capital gains, dividend, inheritance, gift or wealth tax. Federal VAT 5%. Emirate level: land registration fees and municipality fees on rent.
regimes.eligibility: Any legal resident (residence visa, e.g. Golden Visa). No tax status needs to be claimed; tax residence under Cabinet Decision 85/2022 matters only for treaty access and for the home country's exit rules.

capital_gains.summary: No personal income tax and no capital gains tax for individuals. Gains on listed or private shares, bonds and real estate held as personal investments are untaxed.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Natural persons are within UAE Corporate Tax only if they run a business with turnover above AED 1,000,000 in a calendar year; wage, personal investment income and real estate investment income are excluded regardless of amount (Cabinet Decision 49/2023, Art. 2).
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Applies to all individuals, resident or not.
capital_gains.regional_differences: None: there is no emirate-level income tax.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Personal Investment income is excluded from Corporate Tax only if the activity does not require a licence from a UAE licensing authority. Running a licensed business, or trading activity that requires a licence, can bring a natural person into 9% Corporate Tax. Real estate disposals carry emirate land registration fees, not a gains tax: Dubai 4% of value on third-party sales, usually paid by the buyer (PwC); Abu Dhabi commonly reported at 2% (law-firm commentary; not confirmed from an ADREC fee schedule). See the emirate file.

capital_gains.rate_basis: No personal income tax (PwC, Sep 2026). Cabinet Decision 49/2023 Art. 2(2) excludes Personal Investment income and Real Estate Investment income of natural persons from Corporate Tax. All rates 0.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Low risk for a private investor. Investing on personal account that needs no licence is Personal Investment, outside Corporate Tax. A licensed trading or investment-management business would be taxed at 9% above AED 375,000 of profit once turnover exceeds AED 1m.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign gains untaxed. No exit tax.

dividends.summary: Dividends are not taxed in the UAE. The only cost is foreign withholding tax at source; the UAE has about 110 tax treaties but none with the United States, so US dividends held directly suffer 30% US WHT.
dividends.important_exceptions: No UAE-US income tax treaty: US-source dividends paid directly to a UAE resident non-US person bear 30% US withholding. Many UAE families hold US equities through Irish-domiciled UCITS funds (15% US WHT at fund level under the Ireland-US treaty); that is a structuring choice, not a UAE rule.

dividends.rate_basis: No personal income tax; personal investment income excluded from Corporate Tax for natural persons (Cabinet Decision 49/2023).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 0% domestic WHT on dividends paid by UAE companies to non-residents (PwC).
dividends.treaty_network: About 110 double tax treaties in force (PwC list, may be incomplete), covering most of the EU, UK, Switzerland, Japan, Singapore, Canada, China and India. No treaty with the United States. A Tax Residency Certificate from the FTA is needed to claim treaty rates.
dividends.holding_company_notes: UAE companies pay 9% Corporate Tax above AED 375,000; a participation exemption for dividends and gains on qualifying shareholdings exists (conditions not verified in this pass). ADGM/DIFC foundations can be used to hold family assets; tax transparency elections exist for family foundations under the CT law (not verified from a primary source here).

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no recurring tax on financial assets.
wealth_tax.regional_differences: Emirates levy a municipality fee on residential property based on annual rental value (Dubai 5%, generally paid by the tenant, or by the owner-occupier), collected with utility bills.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No property tax on capital value. Dubai municipality fee: 5% of annual rental value for residential property (tenant pays; owner if not rented). Other emirates charge similar fees at their own rates.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. Children inherit tax-free. Forced heirship (Sharia for Muslims; the 2023 civil personal status law for non-Muslims without a will) governs who inherits UAE assets, so registered wills are essential.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: None for the tax exemption. Testamentary freedom for non-Muslims depends on a registered will (DIFC, ADGM, or local court).
inheritance.regional_differences: No emirate levies inheritance tax. Abu Dhabi has its own non-Muslim personal status law (2021) and the ADGM will registry; Dubai has the DIFC Courts Wills Service. Emirate land departments charge registration fees when inherited real estate is transferred into heirs' names (rates per emirate; not verified for inheritance transfers).
inheritance.important_exceptions: MATERIAL PLANNING ISSUE - forced heirship, not tax. (1) Muslims: Sharia fixed shares apply to the estate (sons typically receive twice a daughter's share; spouse and parents have fixed fractions; only up to one third may be left freely by will to non-heirs). A will cannot opt out of this for a Muslim testator. (2) Non-Muslims: since 1 Feb 2023 Federal Decree-Law 41/2022 (civil personal status) applies by default: without a will, 50% to the surviving spouse and 50% split equally among the children regardless of gender; with no children, parents, then siblings (Trowers). Foreign heirs may ask for the law of the deceased's nationality to apply, but not against a registered will (Art. 11(3), per law-firm commentary). Abu Dhabi has had a similar non-Muslim personal status law since 2021 (Abu Dhabi Law No. 14/2021, per Withers); ADGM Courts register non-Muslim wills. (3) Wills: the DIFC Courts Wills Service registers English-language common-law wills (Full Will AED 10,000, mirror wills AED 15,000 for a couple; guardianship clauses for minors resident in Dubai or Ras Al Khaimah). Withers notes the post-2023 rules are recent and untested, that jointly owned assets with a Muslim are subject to Sharia, and that transferring land through trusts or wills is restricted under local law. In practice a non-Muslim family should register wills (DIFC or ADGM) and consider an ADGM/DIFC foundation for the portfolio; bank accounts in the deceased's sole name are commonly frozen until a court succession order (not verified from a primary source). (4) The family's home-country inheritance tax may still apply (e.g. citizenship-based US estate tax, or tails of the former residence country).

inheritance.gift_tax: None. Lifetime gifts to children are not taxed. Gifts of UAE real estate trigger emirate land registration procedures (fees for gifts between relatives not verified).
inheritance.foreign_assets: No UAE tax on foreign assets inherited or gifted. Succession to foreign assets is governed by the law of where they are situated and by the will.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Not relevant for tax. For succession, religion and (for non-Muslim foreigners) the choice of nationality law matter.

residency.tax_residency_test: Cabinet Decision No. 85 of 2022 (in force 1 March 2023), clarified by Ministerial Decision 27/2023: an individual is UAE tax resident if (a) their usual or primary place of residence and centre of financial and personal interests is in the UAE; or (b) they are physically present 183 days or more in a 12-month period; or (c) they are present 90 days or more in a 12-month period, are a UAE/GCC national or hold a UAE residence permit, and have a permanent place of residence or employment/business in the UAE. Part days count as full days. Tax Residency Certificate (FTA via EmaraTax): AED 50 submission fee plus AED 1,000 for an electronic certificate for an individual without a CT number; covers a current or past calendar year or 12-month period, never a future one; processing about 10 business days. Evidence: Emirates ID, passport with official entry/exit report, and for the 90-day and centre-of-interests tests proof of residence/employment/interests.

routes.name: Golden Visa - investor (public investment, e.g. deposit/fund)
routes.requirements: 10-year renewable residence visa per u.ae; minimum capital AED 2,000,000. Can sponsor spouse and children; may stay outside the UAE beyond the usual 6-month limit.

routes.name: Golden Visa - real estate investor
routes.requirements: Property worth at least AED 2,000,000. The federal portal u.ae (updated 28 Jul 2026, citing ICP) lists this category as a 5-year renewable visa (10 years only for public investment); ICP describes Golden Residence as 5 to 10 years. Many advisers and the Dubai Land Department channel describe a 10-year property visa since 2022: the official federal statement is 5 years, so plan on 5 and confirm the term at application. Family can be sponsored.

routes.name: Ordinary investor / employment / company-owner residence
routes.requirements: 2-3 year residence visas through a mainland or free zone company (e.g. a DIFC/ADGM family office entity) or employment. Requires presence at least once every 6 months (not Golden Visa).

corporate.summary: Federal Decree-Law 47/2022, for periods from 1 June 2023: 0% on taxable income up to AED 375,000, 9% above. Qualifying Free Zone Persons pay 0% on qualifying income and 9% on other income. Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax of 15% for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750m+ in two of the four preceding years, for periods starting on or after 1 January 2025 (Cabinet Decision 142/2024). Natural persons are taxed only on licensed business activity with turnover above AED 1m. No withholding tax on dividends paid out.
corporate.special_zones: Free zones (e.g. DMCC, JAFZA) with the 0% QFZP regime subject to substance and de minimis conditions. DIFC (Dubai) and ADGM (Abu Dhabi) are financial free zones with English-language common-law courts, trust and foundation laws, and will registries; they host most single-family offices. Free-zone status does not change personal taxation (already nil).

income.name: United Arab Emirates

income_tax.summary: No federal or emirate-level personal income tax on employment or self-employment income (PwC, reviewed 9 Sep 2026). Non-GCC expatriates pay no UAE social security; only a flat unemployment-insurance fee (AED 5 or 10 a month) applies. A person running a business pays 9% UAE Corporate Tax only if business turnover exceeds AED 1 million.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: No self-employment social security for non-GCC nationals. Self-employment through a licensed business can come under 9% Corporate Tax above AED 1,000,000 turnover; wages and personal investment income do not count toward that turnover.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Dubai has no income-based local tax. Unemployment insurance: AED 5 per month (basic salary up to AED 16,000) or AED 10 per month (above), from 1 Jan 2023.

regimes.name: Dubai Virtual Working Programme (remote work visa)
regimes.description: One-year Dubai residence visa for remote workers employed by or owning a company outside the UAE. Holders live in the UAE with 0% personal income tax because the UAE levies none. Officially reported minimum is USD 5,000 a month; older and third-party sources still quote USD 3,500. Covers local work: the UAE levies no personal income tax at all, so pay for work done while living in the UAE is untaxed (PwC).
regimes.duration_note: Valid for one year, renewable on re-application; no cap on renewals found.

income.residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: no visa-free right to work. A remote worker employed by a non-UAE company, or owning one, can apply for the Dubai Virtual Working Programme (one-year residence visa, reported minimum USD 5,000 a month). A skilled employee normally enters on a UAE work permit and residence visa sponsored by a local employer; the Golden Visa is a longer-term route (see data/jurisdictions/ARE.json). Citizenship does not change the route.
